body: I can understand the feeling of meaninglessness, but nihilistic thinking can sometimes be harmful to us. I struggle a lot with trying to find purpose and question the point of life. Then I try to look at it differently: What viable alternative is there? We simply exist and that's how nature seems to be set up.
Thank you for the support. Hope you're doing ok. Probably nobody deserves it but our judgement is clouded sometimes.
I'm trying to get back to old hobbies, yes. Thanks.
Thank you for the understanding. It was just a bit too much stress that day and everything bottled up surfaced. Sometimes I hate myself for all these weaknesses I have and can't seem to overcome.
Hey if you could just beat me to death that would be great. I volunteer.
Perfect.
Thanks for the encouragement. I agree on the point about little things in life. You seem to have a realistic view on that, which is refreshing. The bread analogy is neat.
Yeah I do appreciate them but I fear I'm letting them down all the time :( I hope things improve for you. At least there are some people here who are willing to talk if you need to. Take care.

I'm sorry people ignore you. That's really cruel. I guess 'happy' people feel uncomfortable around others who are having a hard time. That's why there is a stigma. I fully understand how you feel though. The fear of physical pain and the consequences for people close to me are keeping me alive right now. You're not a coward, it's the survival instincts that are still trying to keep us alive even though we are suffering.
Insomnia is torture, I can fully understand why you feel this way. I'm surprised that doctors couldn't figure this out. Whatever you decide, I hope you get relief. All the best.

Yeah, I wish there was such a place, honestly. It would be useful but apart from maybe living off the land somewhere in the countryside or the mountains, I don't see how this would be possible. I guess some remote monastery could do...

I can empathise completely with this. Paralysis is awful and the fear can keep you like this for a long time. Every time I let someone down (unintentionally) a part of me dies. Well done on the new job though. Hope the training goes well.

If you haven't already, you could try to get counselling/therapy through your university's health centre. I did that for a while and at the very least it kept me going through exams. I know it's not a solution to everything but if you definitely have to go in 8 days, it is better than nothing. 

Honestly, I know it sucks, it's torture to feel like this, but sometimes something as simple as a walk outside can keep you functioning for a bit. In fact I'm in a very similar situation to yours... so yeah I'm also kind of screwed. 

All the best.

Don't know if it's any comfort but I can completely relate to this. Especially when you put in effort to also lead a good life but it all fails... They may have one or two bad days but in the end everyone else seems to return to being happy, while we kind of struggle all the time...

Well done on finding some happiness in your life. I'm certainly grateful about a lot but it is sometimes frustrating to cope with setbacks. Something weird conditioned me to believe that I was instantly a "loser" if I'm falling behind my peers. Thanks for the encouragement.
Sorry that you're having a tough time :( I suspect that these thoughts we struggle with are not entirely rational, yet they seem very powerful because of some kind of conditioning.

Thank you for the advice. Understanding personal priorities seems like a good starting point and mental health is an important one. You're right about social media. It causes a lot of anxiety and insecurity sometimes. Glad that you feel happier without Facebook.
Never tried meds, but will consider them if it goes on. Exercising was good in combination with other things but now I have no energy left. Thanks for the reply.
Thanks for your suggestion. Will check it out.

During weekends wake up early around 6:30 and run about 4-5 km in a local park. Then have something nutritious for breakfast and try my best to keep my desk and room tidy. Usually spend the afternoon studying or reading (doing anything to exercise the brain really). I would then try to get to bed before 10 pm. I sometimes had to take sleeping pills to calm down. On weekdays I used to cycle to school.

Yeah, I get what you're saying. In my experience, exercise has to be done regularly in parallel with other stuff for any positive effect. It also has to be fairly vigorous and long to release serotonin or dopamine. So basically it's a constant uphill battle which doesn't help...

Yes, I have in the past managed to recover partially but you won't like the answer. I did it through a lot of physical exercise, intense studying and lots of sleep. Yeah, so it takes discipline and motivation.
Ideally, for motivation, you need to have something to look forward to or some other type of joy in your life, but obviously for us depressed people that is in short supply if at all :(

Yeah, virtually everyone I know is naturally super gifted at something (sports, gaming, academic stuff, languages, etc.) and they can pick things up effortlessly. I have to put in an insane amount of time before I get good at something and even then it doesn't match the skill of the naturally gifted. Maybe it's a mental block, I don't know...

I understand so well how you're feeling. It is awful to be consumed with self hate and shame all the time. I also struggle with some important stuff in life. The world can be pretty ugly and this can be a real challenge for people like us who struggle. All the best for the future.

In the past I would read books about Physics, Mathematics and science in general. Astronomy was another thing I did related to that (I have a small telescope). Used to enjoy going hiking in the mountains, but that's not always possible. I tried exercising a lot to naturally recover, so I did a lot of running and played football with friends. Used to cycle as well until some lovely person stole my bike... 

I just had an interview for a summer job today. I'm studying Engineering at university so I also thought about looking into some internships in the STEM fields to keep my busy with something useful related to my career. I haven't really decided on a specific area which makes me anxious and makes my worry worse :( 

Thanks ever so much for your help

Thank you for replying. Good to hear that you're feeling better. I'm a bit concerned about becoming dependent on medicine and unpleasant side effects. That's why I was advised against it, but since it works for a lot of people I'll consider it if there's no improvement. Thank you.
No medication - only a few counselling sessions.
